best_for: Windows 10 and 11 and Linux users who want to clear browser caches, logs and temp files without ads or upsells, and who can review a preview before deleting.
description:
BleachBit is a disk cleaner for freeing space and keeping your activity private, developed in the open since 2008. It works offline, with no account to register and no license to activate, and it is translated into 61 languages.

It does more than delete whole files. It can clear the Firefox address history, the LibreOffice recent documents list or the Windows registry's recently used lists and leave the rest of each file alone. It finds scattered Thumbs.db and .DS_Store files, removes Linux language files you never use, and shrinks Firefox and Chrome databases without losing data. On Windows it can load winapp2.ini files for thousands of extra cleaners, and it can run portable from a USB drive.

points.title: Free, with no paid tier
points.text: BleachBit is open source under GPL 3.0. There is no Pro edition to buy and nothing in the app is held back.

points.title: Preview before you delete
points.text: You tick the cleaners you want, run a preview to see what would go, then delete. Cleaners cover Chrome, Edge, Firefox, VLC, system logs, temp files and Linux package caches such as APT, DNF and Pacman.

points.title: Shredding is permanent
points.text: It can shred files and overwrite free disk space so deleted data cannot be read back. That is the point, so there is no undo: check the preview first.

points.title: Scriptable
points.text: A command-line interface lets you run the same cleaning from scripts or scheduled tasks, and custom cleaners can be written in its CleanerML format.

points.title: Windows 7 and 8 stop at 4.7.0
points.text: Version 6.0.6 supports Windows 10 and 11. The project points users of XP, Vista, 7 and 8 to BleachBit 4.7.0. The Windows listing here keeps 11 versions, with 32-bit installers for the current user or the whole machine.

points.title: No Mac app
points.text: There is no macOS download. On Linux the project ships its own .deb and .rpm packages for current Debian, Ubuntu, Mint, Fedora, AlmaLinux and openSUSE releases, plus an AppImage. The Flatpak listed here is not marked verified by Flathub, and only the current release is kept.
